native full-duplex speech, hybrid SSM/MoE, attention kernels, and open video-generation ecosystems
load-bearing papers explicitly absent from the normalized base index because of arXiv result truncation

coverage_findings: The original one-query-per-category retrospective arXiv collector collapsed the six-month paper pool onto December because of descending order plus max_results=200; the Special collector was corrected to calendar-month partitioning before this audit was accepted.
Even after temporal partitioning, all 36 month/category arXiv queries reached max_results=200. The base paper pool is therefore broad but not exhaustive.

The official-page watchlist initially omitted or under-itemized several material actors. The shared watchlist and procedures were broadened, and item-level first-party gap-fill was added without replacing the base intake.
Supplemental pages are preserved as Raw bytes and pass through the same Screening/Evidence boundary as base records; they are not direct editorial insertions.
The v0.3 paper supplement restores 14 load-bearing H2 papers known to be absent because of arXiv truncation; it is not an assertion that every truncated paper was recovered.
residual_limitations: No finite static watchlist or capped arXiv discovery run proves exhaustive capture of every material 2024-H2 event or paper.
Some current vendor index/living pages can omit or relocate historical item-level pages; unresolved chronology must remain bounded by preserved Raw sources and explicit HOLD/claim qualification.
Historical community/X reaction research is disabled for half-year retrospectives and is not part of this Source Intake.
Vendor/project/author benchmark and performance claims are primary-source claims, not independent reproduction.
decision: Coverage is sufficient to proceed to Candidate Selection and Architecture because the canonical base intake was preserved, temporal collapse was repaired, material source-plane gaps were audited and gap-filled through canonical provenance, and remaining incompleteness is explicit rather than silently treated as absence.
